Definition: to be pleased with; specifically, to satisfy a debt
BiblicalUsage: Ratsah is to be pleased with, to delight in, to accept — and by law, to satisfy a debt. The burnt offering 'shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him'; God says of His Servant, 'Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth'; the Proverb says, 'When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him'; and the psalm says, 'The LORD taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.'
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God's pleasure is the deepest truth about Him: He delights in His Servant, He takes pleasure in those who fear Him, and He accepts the offering that makes atonement. And my position is that the whole gospel hangs on this word — that God is pleased, not grudging, toward those who come to Him through the One in whom His soul delights.
